findings.title: canManage() grants global group manage with only VIEW scope
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2, canManage() calls hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an admin who holds only the all-groups VIEW permission passes requireManage(). That check guards creating and moving top-level groups in GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup. The result is privilege escalation from view to manage. It should check MANAGE only.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission looks up resources by id and returns resource ids, not group ids
findings.body: Inside findByType, the method passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission, which calls findByName. V2 resources are named by group id, so the lookup by resource id fails and evaluation falls back to the all-groups resource. It then adds the resource id, not the group id (getName), to the result set. Filtering users by group membership therefore uses the wrong ids. Also, the V2 schema resources are created via resourceStore.create without setType, so findByType('Groups') may return nothing except the type resource itself.

findings.title: Group filter applied even when admin can view users
findings.body: The previous `!auth.users().canView()` guard was removed before setting the UserModel.GROUPS attribute. In V1 this is masked because the method returns an empty set when the admin can view users. However, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission only short-circuits on users().canView(), so this is fragile, and the same change is duplicated in BruteForceUsersResource.
